name: Gemini
introduction: is the Twins, Castor and Pollux, brothers of Helen of Troy and protectors of sailors. Two bright stars mark their heads, and long lines of stars trace their bodies toward Orion. It is a zodiac constellation, best seen on northern winter evenings.

sections.title: What makes it special
paragraphs: Two planets were discovered in Gemini. In 1781, William Herschel found Uranus near [Tejat](hip:30343), the first planet discovered with a telescope. In 1930, Clyde Tombaugh found Pluto near [Wasat](hip:35550).
Every December, the Geminids, the strongest annual meteor shower, radiate from near Castor. Unusually, their source is not a comet but the rocky asteroid 3200 Phaethon.

sections.title: Notable stars
paragraphs: [Pollux](hip:37826), 34 light-years away, is an orange giant with a giant planet, and the brighter of the twins. [Castor](hip:36850), 51 light-years away, is one of the most complex systems known: through a telescope it appears as two stars, but there are six stars in three pairs.
[Alhena](hip:31681) marks the twins’ feet. [Mebsuta](hip:32246) is a yellow supergiant, and [Mekbuda](hip:34088) a Cepheid variable that pulsates every ten days.

sections.title: Beyond the stars
paragraphs: The open cluster M35 is visible to the naked eye on dark nights. The Eskimo Nebula is a planetary nebula that looks like a face in a fur hood. [Geminga](id:psr-j0633p1746), about 800 light-years away, is a nearby neutron star that shines powerfully in gamma rays and is one of the remains of supernovae that exploded near the Sun.
